name: Challenge: Practice Return restores artwork and Redo; Keep creates a separate reloadable project
description: Exercise the compiled local PixiBun build through user controls. Use a desktop viewport. Compare actual artwork and persistent state, not only element visibility. Missing prerequisites or unobservable cancellation must be reported rather than silently skipped.

planSteps.description: Navigate to /studio.
Verify restoration has finished and the main drawing canvas is editable.
Rename the project to Challenge original using the project-name control and confirm with Enter.
Select the Pen tool.
Draw a short horizontal stroke in the upper-left quarter of the drawing canvas, away from its borders.
Draw a separate short vertical stroke in the lower-right quarter of the drawing canvas.
Verify both strokes exist with transparent space between them; remember their positions and shapes for later comparisons.
Click Undo.
Verify only the horizontal stroke remains and Redo is enabled.
Click Return to PixiBun Home.
Click Playground in the home navigation.
Click Trace Stencil.
Verify recognizable stencil artwork appears and differs from the original single horizontal stroke.
Click Return to drawing.
Verify the Studio project is Challenge original with only its horizontal stroke; Redo remains enabled.
Click Redo.
Verify both strokes exist with transparent space between them; remember their positions and shapes for later comparisons.
Click Return to PixiBun Home.
Click Playground in the home navigation.
Click Trace Stencil.
Click Keep practice in Studio.
Verify Studio contains the traced practice artwork under a name different from Challenge original.
Reload this page.
Verify the kept practice artwork restores successfully with its separate project name.
Open File, then Projects.
Open project Challenge original.
Verify both original strokes return unchanged; kept practice has not overwritten the original project.
